?? Role Purpose
As a Metal Fabricator/Welder at Bowhill Engineering, you’ll play a key role in delivering precision-fabricated, heavy structural steel components for some of the nation’s most important infrastructure projects. Working in our multiple workshops, you’ll bring your technical expertise, pride in workmanship, and team spirit to every task. ?? What Does Great Look Like?
Success in this role means showing up with a can-do attitude, working efficiently and safely, and being proud of the work you produce. A high-performing Metal Fabricator at Bowhill:

? Works well under pressure and adapts to varying project demands
? Upholds safety, quality, and productivity standards
? Supports their teammates and contributes to a positive culture
? Seeks improvement and development in their trade
 
? What You’ll Bring
• Trade Qualification minimum 2 years preferred (Cert III in Engineering – Fabrication/Welding or equivalent) or relevant welding experience 
• Strong attention to detail and commitment to quality
• Ability to interpret technical drawings and specifications
• Fit-for-work attitude and high personal standards
• Team spirit and accountability for your own work and results
 
?? Why Work With Us?
At Bowhill Engineering, we don’t just build structures—we build futures. You’ll be part of a company that invests in cutting-edge facilities, meaningful projects, and the people who make them happen. We take pride in our culture and work hard to ensure every team member feels supported and valued.
 
?? Employee Benefits – Why Bowhill?

• Relocation Incentive / Accommodation Assistance available *(conditions apply)

• Reward & Recognition Initiatives
• Social Events & Team Activities
• Career Development & Training Opportunities
• Modern Workshop Facilities with Annual Wage Reviews
 
?? How to Apply
?? Contact: Samantha Krollig, HR Manager – 08 8570 4208
?? Apply via the Bowhill Engineering website – job vacancies page. Resume & 3 x References required.
??? Weld Test required as part of the interview process.

result.description:
We are a leader in ECEC, sponsoring a range of Early Childhood Education and Care services. We are a not-for-profit organisation with a strong heritage in early childhood education in Queensland and Australia. We value excellence, inclusion, engagement and integrity in our work with children, families and communities and supporting a professional and capable staff team.

Every career helps children thrive in enriched and nurturing learning environments, and we want the same for you. By joining our team, you’ll play a vital role in shaping a child’s life journey, both during their time with us and beyond. Our achievements are made possible by dedicated professionals like you and we are dedicated to your success, providing a range of benefits, programs, and opportunities to support your growth, well-being, and career development.

The safety and wellbeing of children is our highest priority, and we are committed to creating environments where every child feels safe, respected, supported and empowered.

About the Role
We are seeking an experienced Capital Works Project Manager to lead the delivery of the 2026-2027 Kindergarten Capital Works Upgrade Program.

Funded by the Queensland Department of Education, this exciting program will support community kindergartens across Queensland to undertake capital upgrades that strengthen child safety, improve supervision and security, and implement the National Child Safety Reforms.

This is a unique opportunity to combine project management, stakeholder engagement and governance to deliver meaningful improvements for children and communities throughout Queensland.

This role is full time, on a fixed-term contract until 30 June 2027, aligned with the Department of Education Capital Works Upgrade Program. Regular travel throughout Queensland will be required to support project delivery and stakeholder engagement.

Key Responsibilities
Manage the Capital Works Upgrade Program from application through to project completion.
Assess funding applications against program eligibility and assessment criteria.
Provide advice to services on project scope, procurement requirements and funding conditions.
Develop project plans, budgets, milestones and risk management strategies.
Monitor project progress, expenditure and compliance with funding agreements.
Coordinate building reports, quotations, approvals, licences and project documentation.
Liaise with builders, contractors, local councils and regulatory authorities.
Conduct site visits across Queensland to monitor project delivery.
Manage project risks and provide timely escalation where required.
Prepare reports for Executive Leadership and the Department of Education.
Ensure all projects meet contractual obligations, funding requirements and record keeping standards.
Support services through practical project management advice and governance throughout delivery.

What we Offer
Work for one of Queensland’s most respected not-for-profit organisations.
Flexible working arrangements
Grow your career and experience with professional development opportunities
Enjoy a competitive wage determined by experience
Prioritise your well-being with our Employee Assistance Program (EAP)
Take time for yourself with an annual Wellbeing Day, on top of your standard leave entitlements.
Celebrate your milestones with an Anniversary Day Off each year.
Enjoy time to recharge with a career that comes with a built-in Christmas holiday break.
Opportunity to contribute to positive outcomes for children, families and communities.

About You
You are an organised project professional who enjoys working collaboratively and solving problems. You can confidently manage multiple projects while building strong relationships with diverse stakeholders.

You will ideally have:
Demonstrated experience managing building or minor capital works projects.
Strong project planning, budgeting and contract management experience.
Experience managing multiple concurrent projects.
Excellent stakeholder engagement and communication skills.
Strong understanding of procurement and contractor management.
High level organisational and documentation skills.
Ability to interpret funding agreements, policies and compliance requirements.
Current Queensland Driver Licence and willingness to travel.

Desirable however not essential:
Qualification in Project Management, Construction Management, Engineering, Architecture or a related discipline.
Experience working within education, local government, community or not-for-profit sectors.
Knowledge of Queensland building approval processes.
Understanding of child-safe environments and risk management.
Experience administering government grant-funded projects.

Success in this role
You will successfully deliver a statewide portfolio of capital works projects by:
Ensuring projects meet funding objectives and contractual requirements.
Supporting services to successfully complete projects within budget and timeframes.
Maintaining strong governance, financial oversight and compliance.
Building positive relationships with affiliate services and contractors.
Providing high-quality reporting and project assurance to Executive Leadership and the Department of Education.

We are committed to building an inclusive workforce. We strongly encourage applications from Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander peoples and individuals from culturally diverse backgrounds.

If this sounds like the right role for you, take the next step and apply now via SEEK!

We appreciate all applicants, though only those selected for an interview will be contacted.

Employer questions
Your application will include the following questions:
Which of the following statements best describes your right to work in Australia?
How many years' experience do you have as a Capital Works Project Manager?
How many years of project management experience do you have?
Have you worked in a role where you were responsible for budget management & forecasting?
Do you have a current Australian driver's licence?
Have you completed a qualification in project management?
How many years' experience do you have with contracts administration?
Do you have a current Working With Children (WWC) Check?

Full-Time: Immediate start
Reports to: Manager
Job Title: Beef Cattle Farm Worker
Salary range: $80,000 - $100,000 + Superannuation & other – depending on skill level
Job Closure date: 30 days

About The Role
On behalf of our client, a progressive and data-driven Angus seed stock operation in the Great Southern region, we are seeking a dedicated and skilled Beef Cattle Farm Worker. This is not just a farmhand role; it is an opportunity to contribute to a strategic breeding program focused on excellence.
Our client has meticulously built a renowned breeding herd over the past decade, with a core philosophy of combining superior genetics with functional, structurally sound cattle. They are committed to advancing their herd through rigorous data-driven selection and a steadfast focus on traits that deliver real profitability and reliability for their commercial bull customers.
We are looking for an individual who is passionate about modern, sustainable beef production and possesses a keen eye for animal detail. The successful candidate will play a hands-on role in the daily care and strategic management of this high-value stud herd, ensuring the highest standards of animal welfare, pasture health, and operational efficiency are maintained.

Key Responsibilities & Duties:
Livestock Care & Health Management
• Conduct daily inspections of cattle to monitor health, behaviour, and well-being, promptly reporting any signs of illness, injury, or distress.
• Feed and water management: Ensure cattle receive balanced nutrition by distributing feed, maintaining feeding schedules, and keeping water troughs clean and functional.
• Assist with veterinary procedures, including vaccinations, drenching, tagging, and administering medications under supervision.
• Support calving operations, assisting with birthing when necessary and ensuring newborn calves receive proper care.
• Assist in breeding programs, including heat detection, artificial insemination (if applicable), and record-keeping.

Grazing & Pasture Management
• Rotational grazing: Move cattle between paddocks to optimize pasture usage, prevent overgrazing, and promote forage regrowth.
• Monitor pasture conditions, identifying weed infestations, soil erosion, or fencing issues that may affect livestock movement.
• Assist in silage/hay production (if applicable), including cutting, baling, and storage for winter feed.

Farm Maintenance & Equipment Operation
• Perform routine repairs on fences, gates, cattle yards, and handling facilities to ensure structural integrity and livestock safety.
• Maintain and clean feeding systems, water pumps, and irrigation equipment to prevent blockages or malfunctions.
• Operate farm machinery (tractors, ATVs, feed mixers, etc.) for feeding, spraying, or pasture maintenance (training provided if needed).
• Assist with weed and pest control to maintain a safe and productive grazing environment.

Cattle Handling & Movement
• Safely mustering, drafting, and sorting cattle using low-stress handling techniques.
• Assist with loading/unloading livestock for transport, sales, or processing, ensuring compliance with animal welfare standards.
• Participate in branding, tagging, and weighing operations as part of herd management.

Record-Keeping & Compliance
• Maintain accurate livestock records, including health treatments, breeding, and weight data.
• Follow biosecurity protocols to prevent disease spread between livestock or properties.
• Adhere to workplace health and safety regulations, including safe chemical handling and machinery use.

Requirements & Qualifications:
• Minimum 1 year of experience in beef cattle farming, livestock handling, or a related agricultural role.
• Strong animal husbandry skills with an understanding of cattle behaviour, nutrition, and health needs.
• Farm machinery experience (tractors, quad bikes, feed wagons) is highly desirable.
• Basic mechanical skills for minor repairs and maintenance of farm infrastructure.
• Valid driver’s license (truck or tractor license is a plus).
• Flexibility to work early mornings, weekends, and public holidays as required by seasonal demands.
• Team player with strong communication skills and the ability to follow instructions.
• Certification in Livestock Production, Agriculture, or Animal Science if preferable but not required.

How to Apply:
Interested candidates should submit a resume and brief cover letter outlining their experience and suitability for the role.

Please note: We are acting as recruitment agents on behalf of our client. Employer details will be provided to shortlisted candidates.

 Position                         Quality Assurance Manager

About AMO Facility Management
AMO Facility Management is a leading provider of integrated facility management services across Australia. Our reputation is built on delivering safe, sustainable, and high-quality outcomes for our clients — outcomes that are underpinned by a certified Integrated Management System spanning ISO 9001:2015, ISO 45001:2018, and ISO 14001:2015. We hold ourselves to the highest standards because our clients depend on it. This role sits at the heart of that commitment.
The Role
Reporting to the Head of Operations, the Quality Assurance Manager holds accountability for the design, implementation, and continual improvement of AMO's Integrated Management System. This is a leadership position that carries real authority and genuine impact — you will shape the quality, safety, and environmental culture of the business. You will work across all levels of the organisation to ensure compliance with our ISO obligations, prepare for and manage certification audits, and build the internal capability that sustains excellence over time.
Job Duties
1.	Develop, implement and continuously improve the organisation’s Integrated Management System (IMS) in accordance with ISO 9001:2015, ISO 45001:2018 and ISO 14001:2015 standards. 
2.	Plan, direct and coordinate quality assurance, environmental and occupational health and safety systems across commercial cleaning and facility management operations to ensure compliance with company policies, client requirements and regulatory obligations. 
3.	Establish and maintain documented quality management procedures, inspection protocols, audit programs, reporting frameworks, corrective action processes and document control systems to support operational consistency and compliance. 
4.	Lead the implementation and ongoing application of the Plan-Do-Check-Act (PDCA) methodology to drive continuous improvement initiatives across quality, safety and environmental management activities. 
5.	Monitor operational performance through regular site inspections, internal audits, compliance reviews and quality assessments to ensure service delivery standards, safety expectations and environmental objectives are consistently achieved. 
6.	Manage non-conformances, incidents, corrective and preventive actions (CAPA), root cause investigations and risk mitigation strategies to improve operational performance and minimise organisational risk. 
7.	Coordinate hazard identification, risk assessments, incident reporting and workplace safety initiatives to ensure all operational activities comply with applicable occupational health and safety requirements. 
8.	Identify and evaluate environmental aspects, impacts and compliance obligations, and implement strategies to support sustainable operational practices and environmental performance targets. 
9.	Prepare for, coordinate and manage internal and external certification audits, including ISO surveillance and recertification audits, and oversee audit close-out actions and compliance reporting. 
10.	Maintain accurate quality, safety and environmental records, including audit findings, compliance documentation, training records, contractor assessments and operational performance reports. 
11.	Liaise with clients, contractors, suppliers, site supervisors and operational personnel to ensure quality expectations, contractual obligations and compliance standards are effectively communicated and maintained. 
12.	Analyse quality and compliance data, audit outcomes, incident trends and operational reports to identify improvement opportunities, strengthen governance controls and support strategic decision-making. 
13.	Develop and deliver staff training, quality awareness programs and compliance initiatives to ensure employees understand organisational procedures, safety responsibilities and quality assurance requirements. 
14.	Lead, mentor and support quality assurance personnel and operational teams to build organisational capability, improve compliance culture and promote continuous improvement across all business operations. 
15.	Prepare and present reports to senior management on IMS performance, compliance status, audit outcomes, risk management activities and ongoing improvement initiatives.
Skills, Qualifications, and Experience Required
•	A bachelor's degree, with at least one year of relevant experience 
•	Strong knowledge of quality management systems, industry standards, safety regulations, and compliance requirements, with proven ability to implement and monitor quality processes
•	Communication and interpersonal skills 
•	Team leading capabilities
